published_statement: As restated (Hill-Solon 1409.8290 eq.(39), READ by sibling audit): <O'_Q>/m_N = (1/(3 beta_0^(nf))){2 - 2 lambda} + (alpha_s^(nf+1)(mu_Q)/pi)(1/(3 beta_0^(nf)))^2 {57/2 - 321 lambda/2 + 8 n_f} + O(alpha_s^2), whose O(alpha_s^0) term at n_f = 3 is SVZ's f_TQ = (2/27)(1 - lambda), lambda = sum_{u,d,s} f_Tq; eq.(101): 'the leading-order alpha_s result is well-known from Ref. [81]' (SVZ). EOS as quoted by the tree (massform.py:1353-1354): 'f_N/m_N = sum_{q=u,d,s} f_Tq alpha_3q/m_q + (2/27) f_TG sum_{q=c,b,t} alpha_3q/m_q ... f_TG = 1 - sum_{q=u,d,s} f_Tq (12)'. Ji's restatement: heavy quarks 'contribute to the mass term, the kinetic and potential energy term, and the trace anomaly term ... their contributions cancel each other in the limit of m_f -> infinity'.
published_hypotheses: Leading order in alpha_s: the heavy-quark theorem m_Q QbarQ -> -(2/3)(alpha_s/8pi) G^2 (= -(alpha_s/12pi) G^2) and the one-loop beta coefficient b_0 = 11 - 2n_f/3 (Hill-Solon eq.(39) O(alpha_s^0); eq.(101)).
Heavy-quark limit: m_Q >> Lambda_QCD, power corrections O(1/m_Q) dropped (Hill-Solon: O(1/m_c) not estimated).
Three light flavours u, d, s define f_TG = 1 - sum_{u,d,s} f_Tq (EOS eq.(12) as quoted); c, b, t decoupled sequentially.

Forward nucleon matrix element of the QCD trace (m_N = <N|theta^mu_mu|N>), QCD only; a COUPLING (the Higgs-nucleon scalar coupling), not a partition of the mass -- the source context is Higgs-nucleon interaction / dark-matter scattering.

lacked_data: What SVZ (1978) lacked: (i) higher-order QCD coefficients (decoupling to O(alpha_s^3): Chetyrkin-Kniehl-Steinhauser 1997; the f_Q series: Hill-Solon 2014); (ii) any non-perturbative charm matrix element (lattice f_Tc from 2012 on; ETM 19 107(22) MeV); (iii) precise light sigma terms (FLAG 2024; still in 2.7 sigma tension). EOS (2008) lacked (ii) and the Hill-Solon series. Does having them change the conclusion? EVIDENCE: the LO relation is a correct LO theorem -- re-derived here from the anomaly and matching, no counterexample exists; beyond-LO moves each f_TQ upward by 2-9% and the coupling sum by +3.3/+3.8%, and breaks the exact (1 - f_l) factorisation; the lattice charm value sits 2.05 sigma above LO. So the new data NARROW the relation's exactness (LO, heavy-limit) but do not refute it, and no conclusion the tree rests on it moves: the coupling rows are CONTESTED and never added to the READ rows (massform.py:354-356), and every coupling-row central value stays below one half (0.3066 -> 0.3169; all-rows 0.3090 -> 0.3193). M's hypothesis is CONFIRMED in its weak form for this result (the authors lacked data that moves the numbers) and NOT confirmed in its strong form (nothing here makes the relation wrong).
grade_evidence: (1) Algebra: sympy re-derives f_TQ = (2/27)(1 - f_l) per heavy quark and the coupling sum 2/9 + (7/9)f_l from the LO anomaly and SVZ decoupling (anomaly matching 7 + 2 = 9 checked); the tree's 0.3066, 0.2944 and 0.3090 reproduce to 4 d.p. from its READ inputs. (2) But the relation holds on the leading-order, heavy-quark-limit class, and the tree drops both qualifiers: 'EXACT' (massform.py:1807, 1812), 'checked exactly over Fraction' (massform.py:351), 'for each of c, b, t' with no 1/m_c hypothesis (massform.py:347-348). Beyond LO (Hill-Solon O(alpha_s^3), READ by the sibling audit, eq.(61) reproduced here) the coupling sum is 0.3169 / 0.3055 (+3.3% / +3.8%), and ETM 19's charm is 2.05 sigma above LO -- a discrepancy, not a refutation. (3) Not WRONG: no counterexample; 2/27 is the correct LO coefficient. Not DATA-DEPENDENT: the LO value uses no datum; the moving datum (sigma-term tension, alpha_s) shifts numbers by <= 0.012, never across one half, and the tree already prints both FLAG readings. Not STANDS: 'exact' is used where the source result is LO. what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree names the LO-in-alpha_s and heavy-quark-limit hypotheses at massform.py:347-351 and drops 'EXACT' at :1807/:1812 (or cites the beyond-LO series), since then statement and hypotheses match the source as used. To OPEN (reading half): a re-read of EOS 0801.3656 p.5 eq.(10) finding it differs from the tree's quote at massform.py:1353-1354 would require re-grading. To WRONG: only a computed contradiction of the LO coefficient -- none exists (anomaly matching fixes 2/27 given b0 = 11 - 2n_f/3). To DATA-DEPENDENT: a coupling-row central value reaching one half under a moved datum, which would need f_Tc ~ 0.26 (sigma_c ~ 245 MeV) -- ~6 sigma above ETM 19's 107(22) MeV.
